# Axis Midcap Fund: Direct Plan, Growth Option (final report)

*Personal research, not SEBI-registered investment advice. Past returns do not guarantee future returns.*

Scheme: Axis Midcap Fund, Direct Plan, Growth Option, AMFI code 120505, NAV ₹138.78 on 2026-09-28 [C1952].

## Verdict box

| Field | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **HOLD**: keep existing holdings and SIPs, do not add fresh lump sums, and put new mid-cap money into a stronger or cheaper alternative |
| **Suits** | Existing holders with a horizon of five years or more and a Very High risk appetite [C2082], who can sit through a fall of about 30% (worst 10-year drawdown -29.36% [C1986]) |
| **Confidence** | Medium. The NAV record, costs and portfolio mix are verified. Trailing benchmark returns, the formal category rank and the fund's own Sharpe ratio are not, so they are left out |
| **What would change it** | Move to SWITCH if the AMC factsheet shows the fund behind the BSE Midcap 150 TRI [C2015] on both 3- and 5-year returns, or if its 5-year CAGR (12.76% [C1955]) is still the lowest of the named peers at the next half-yearly review. Move to SIP ONLY if rolling returns climb back above the peers and the benchmark while the team stays stable under the new CIO [C2019] |

## Snapshot

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Equity Scheme – Mid Cap Fund. SEBI requires at least 65% of assets in mid-cap stocks [C1976] |
| AMC | Axis Mutual Fund. Lead manager Shreyash Devalkar since 2016-11-23 [C2060] |
| Plan and option | Direct Plan, Growth Option, AMFI code 120505 [C1952] |
| Latest NAV | ₹138.78 on 2026-09-28 [C1952] |
| AUM | ₹35,425.07 crore as of 2026-08-31 [C1968] |
| TER | Direct 0.84% as of 2026-09-27 [C1961]; Regular 1.79% [C1962] |
| Benchmark | BSE Midcap 150 TRI [C2015]; no benchmark change, merger or change to the scheme's fundamental attributes found for 2024–26 [C2061] |
| Riskometer | Very High [C2082] |

## Performance

**Trailing returns (AMFI NAV, annualised, to 2026-09-28):** 1 year 7.17% [C1953], 3 years 15.50% [C1954], 5 years 12.76% [C1955].

**Against the benchmark.** The only verified comparison is since inception, from the AMC's own page as of 2026-01-30: fund 18.68% a year against 18.03% for the BSE Midcap 150 TRI [C2077][C2078]. After more than a decade of active fees, the lead is thin. The AMC's live page also shows trailing benchmark returns. But the fund returns on that same page do not match the AMFI-computed returns, and the factsheet PDF could not be read to settle the difference. Those benchmark figures, and the gaps worked out from them, are still under review and are left out of this report.

**Peer comparison (Direct Growth, AMFI NAV, to 2026-09-28):**

| Scheme | 1 year | 3 years | 5 years |
|---|---|---|---|
| Axis Midcap | 7.17% [C1953] | 15.50% [C1954] | 12.76% [C1955] |
| Edelweiss Mid Cap | 7.24% [C2031] | 19.51% [C2034] | 17.98% [C2036] |
| Nippon India Growth Mid Cap | 7.68% [C2039] | 17.15% [C2042] | 17.38% [C2043] |
| HDFC Mid Cap | 6.17% [C2045] | 15.96% [C2048] | 18.12% [C2090] |
| Motilal Oswal Midcap | 0.61% [C2110] | 17.61% [C2111] | 20.35% [C2112] |
| Kotak Mid Cap | 4.97% [C2113] | 16.29% [C2114] | 16.11% [C2115] |
| ITI Mid Cap | 11.06% UNVERIFIED [C2116] | under review, omitted | 15.82% [C2118] |
| Axis Nifty Midcap 50 Index (passive) | 8.36% [C2065] | 14.00% [C2067] | n/a, launched 2022-03-31 [C2062] |

- **5 years:** Axis's 12.76% [C1955] is the lowest of the seven active funds in the table. The others range from 15.82% [C2118] to 20.35% [C2112].
- **3 years:** Axis's 15.50% [C1954] is below every named active peer with a verified figure, from HDFC's 15.96% [C2048] to Edelweiss's 19.51% [C2034]. It is ahead of the passive index fund's 14.00% [C2067].
- **1 year:** 7.17% [C1953] is mid-table. It trails the AMC's own index fund at 8.36% [C2065].
- The peers are a hand-picked set of large, well-known mid-cap funds, not the whole category. The formal category rank, quartile and medians are still under review and are left out.

**Rolling 3-year returns (5 years to 2026-09-28):** worst 13.91% [C1956], median 18.99% [C1957], best 25.89% [C1958] a year. Because even the worst window was positive, every 3-year holding period in the last 5 years made money [C2026]. The 10-year rolling figures are still under review and are left out. The 10-year maximum drawdown of -29.36% [C1986] shows the longer record includes harsher periods.

**Market phases (point-to-point NAV change, not annualised):**

| Phase | Window | NAV change |
|---|---|---|
| Mid-cap bear phase | 2018-01-15 to 2019-01-16 | +1.39% [C1992] |
| Covid crash | 2020-01-20 to 2020-03-19 | -20.31% [C1995] |
| 2021 rally | 2021-01-14 to 2022-01-13 | +41.36% [C1997] |
| 2022 correction | 2021-11-16 to 2023-03-13 | -10.44% [C1999] |
| Mid-cap boom | 2023-03-13 to 2024-09-12 | +82.04% [C2001] |
| Correction | 2024-09-12 to 2025-03-11 | -15.67% [C2003][C2081] |
| Recovery | 2025-03-11 to 2026-09-28 | +24.05% [C2005] |

**Recent stretch.** From 2024-09-12 to 2026-09-28 the fund grew only about 2.24% a year [C2101], below the 5.39% 91-day T-bill rate [C1984]. The NAV is -4.89% below its 2026-08-31 high of ₹145.91 [C2008][C1989].

**Direct vs Regular.** Over 5 years the Regular Plan returned 11.53% a year [C1966], against 12.76% for the Direct Plan [C1955].

**SIP outcome.** Not computed. The fincalc toolkit has no SIP or XIRR function, and the house rules forbid hand calculation, so SIP returns are UNVERIFIED.

## Risk

| Measure (Axis Midcap, Direct Growth) | Value |
|---|---|
| Annualised volatility, 5 years | 14.60% [C1959] |
| Maximum drawdown, 5 years | -20.34% [C1960] |
| Maximum drawdown, 10 years | -29.36% [C1986] |
| Covid crash, monthly sample points | -20.3% [C1987] |
| Current fall from the 2026-08-31 high | -4.89% [C2008] |

The 10-year drawdown is almost 9 points deeper than the 5-year one [C1986][C1960]. Anyone judging risk from 5-year statistics alone would understate the tail risk. The exact dates of that trough could not be found, because the tool returns only monthly sample points.

**Risk-adjusted returns.** The risk-free rate used is the 91-day T-bill cut-off yield of 5.39% a year from a September 2026 RBI auction [C1984]. The fund's own AMFI-derived Sharpe and Sortino ratios are still under review, so they are withheld. A secondary source (Tickertape, as on 2026-09-25) shows a standard deviation of 14.29 [C2083] and a Sharpe ratio of 0.35 [C2084]. Its risk-free rate is not stated, so these are not comparable with the peer figures below. The AMC's page shows a standard deviation of 16.15% and a beta of 0.86 (UNVERIFIED) [C1983].

Peer figures below cover 2021-09-20 to 2026-09-28 at the same 5.39% risk-free rate [C1984]. All are UNVERIFIED:

| Scheme | Volatility | Max drawdown | Sharpe | Sortino |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Axis Midcap | 14.60% [C1959] | -20.34% [C1960] | withheld | withheld |
| Edelweiss Mid Cap | 16.41% [C2006] | -20.06% [C2007] | 0.794 [C2009] | 1.069 [C2133] |
| Nippon India Growth Mid Cap | 16.24% [C2124] | -19.87% [C2125] | 0.774 [C2126] | 1.039 [C2127] |
| ITI Mid Cap | 16.84% [C2010] | -22.66% [C2011] | 0.675 [C2012] | 0.889 [C2132] |
| Motilal Oswal Midcap | 17.18% [C2128] | withheld | 0.873 [C2130] | 1.232 [C2131] |
| HDFC Mid Cap | withheld | withheld | 0.851 [C2122] | 1.149 [C2123] |

Axis has the lowest volatility of the funds with figures, and its 5-year drawdown is about the same as Edelweiss's and Nippon's [C1960][C2007][C2125]. So lower volatility has not meant noticeably smaller losses. Every peer with a figure shows a Sharpe ratio of at least 0.675 [C2012]. Axis's matching figure is not verified, so no Sharpe ranking is claimed.

## Portfolio and style

- **Market-cap mix (as of 2026-08-31):** mid caps 68.4% [C1970], large caps 18.82% [C1972], small caps 5.58% [C1974]. That clears the SEBI 65% minimum [C1976], but with little room to spare.
- **Asset mix:** equity 92.8%, mutual fund units 0.88%, debt and cash 6.32% [C1975].
- **Concentration:** the top 10 holdings are 26.39% of the portfolio, and the largest, Federal Bank, is 4.4% [C1977][C1978]. Sources disagree on the number of holdings, between 91 and 95 (UNVERIFIED) [C1982].
- **Sectors:** Financial Services 21.08%, Capital Goods 14.33%, Auto and Auto Components 12.76%, Consumer Services 11.8%, Healthcare 10.15% [C1979].
- **Turnover:** 0.81x on the AMC's page against 0.55x on AdvisorKhoj, an unresolved conflict [C1980].
- **Style:** bottom-up selection of quality, high-conviction mid-caps with moats and steady cash flows [C2047]. Press commentary (opinion) blames the fund's lag since about 2023 on an NBFC-heavy "quality" tilt [C2033]. The AMC's former CIO described "quality and growth" as the cornerstones of its approach while widening the stock universe from 328 to 450 names [C2050].
- **Not available:** portfolio P/E and P/B, overlap with peers or the index, style drift over the last 12 to 24 months, and any foreign, derivative or unlisted exposure. All are UNVERIFIED.

## Costs, loads and taxes

- **TER, as of 2026-09-27:** Direct 0.84% [C1961][C1981], Regular 1.79% [C1962]. The gap is 0.95 percentage points a year (fincalc, from inputs [C1961][C1962]).
- **Against the AMC's own index fund:** the Axis Nifty Midcap 50 Index Fund (Direct) charges 0.29% [C1965], 0.55 percentage points a year less than this fund (fincalc, from inputs [C1961][C1965]).
- **Exit load:** 1% on units redeemed within 3 months of allotment, above a 10% free allowance; nil after that [C1963]. An addendum dated 2026-06-05 cut the load period from 12 months to 3 months, effective 2026-06-15 [C2072].
- **Minimum investment:** ₹100 lump sum and monthly SIP; ₹10 daily SIP [C1964].
- **Tax (UNVERIFIED, from tax-advisory sites, not the Finance Act):** short-term gains (held up to 12 months) taxed at 20%. Long-term gains taxed at 12.5% on the amount above ₹1.25 lakh a year under Section 112A [C1967].
- **Peer TERs (UNVERIFIED, aggregators disagree):** HDFC about 0.76%, Kotak about 0.38%, ITI about 0.57%, Nippon about 1.15%, Motilal about 0.95% [C1969].
- **10-year cost of Regular vs Direct:** not computed, because fincalc has no compounding function.

## Management and AMC

- **Fund managers:** Shreyash Devalkar (lead) since 2016-11-23 [C2060], Nitin Arora since 2023-08-03 [C2063], Krishnaa N since 2024-03-01 [C2064]. No change to the managers in the last 90 days (UNVERIFIED) [C2024]. The whole 10-year record sits under one lead manager.
- **CIO:** on 2026-03-05 the AMC named R Sivakumar as CIO, succeeding Ashish Gupta, who had been CIO since March 2023 [C2019]. It is too early to see any effect on this fund's process.
- **Left out because still under review:** the 2023 departure of the head of equities, the list of other schemes the lead manager runs and their rankings, the exact dates of the 2022 dismissals, and whether the AMC CEO's term has been renewed.

## News and events

- **Front-running case:** SEBI issued its final order in the Axis MF front-running matter on 2026-07-24, closing the case subject to appeal [C2017]. The press reports that the former chief dealer was barred for 7 years and fined ₹3 crore (UNVERIFIED) [C2058]. The claim that SEBI found no wrongdoing by the AMC itself is still under review and is not relied on here.
- **Scheme changes:** the only one found is the exit-load change of 2026-06-05 [C2072]. No benchmark change or merger was found [C2061].
- **Category flows (UNVERIFIED, industry-wide, not fund-specific):** mid-cap funds took in a net ₹6,989.40 crore in August 2026 [C2052], and monthly SIP contributions reached about ₹32,297 crore [C2055]. There is no sign of a category-wide outflow, but this fund's own flows could not be isolated.
- **September fall:** the NAV fell -4.89% after 2026-08-31 [C2008]. Press stories blaming a single holding and a broad index fall could not be verified and are left out.

## Bull vs bear

**Bull case.** The fund is steady and sticks to its mandate. The worst rolling 3-year return in the last 5 years was 13.91% a year [C1956]. Volatility is lower than the peers with data [C1959]. The lead manager has been in place for 10 years [C2060]. Direct costs are fair at 0.84% [C1961], and the fund is ahead of its benchmark since inception, 18.68% vs 18.03% [C2077][C2078]. For a SIP investor who values a smoother ride, that steadiness is worth something.

**Bear case.** The steadiness has cost too much return. The fund's 5-year CAGR of 12.76% [C1955] is the lowest of the seven active funds compared, against 20.35% for Motilal Oswal [C2112] and 18.12% for HDFC [C2090]. Recent growth, about 2.24% a year since 2024-09-12 [C2101], has been below the T-bill rate [C1984]. The AMC's own index fund costs 0.29% [C1965] and returned more over the last year, 8.36% vs 7.17% [C2065][C1953]. The AMC's investment leadership also changed recently [C2019].

**Weighing them.** The bull case explains why existing holders need not rush out. The bear case explains why new money has better homes. That is why the verdict is HOLD.

## Alternatives in the category

- **Axis Nifty Midcap 50 Index Fund (Direct):** TER 0.29% [C1965], 3-year return 14.00% [C2067]. The cheapest option at the same AMC, but it tracks a narrower 50-stock index [C2062].
- **HDFC Mid Cap (Direct):** 5-year return 18.12% [C2090], 3-year 15.96% [C2048].
- **Edelweiss Mid Cap (Direct):** 3-year return 19.51% [C2034], 5-year 17.98% [C2036].
- **Nippon India Growth Mid Cap (Direct):** 5-year return 17.38% [C2043]; the aggregator TER looks higher (UNVERIFIED) [C1969].
- **Motilal Oswal Midcap (Direct):** best 5-year return, 20.35% [C2112], but only 0.61% over 1 year [C2110] and the highest volatility, 17.18% (UNVERIFIED) [C2128].
- **Kotak Mid Cap (Direct):** 5-year return 16.11% [C2115]; aggregator TER about 0.38% (UNVERIFIED) [C1969].
- **A broad Midcap 150 index fund:** gives benchmark-like exposure (BSE Midcap 150 TRI [C2015]) at index-fund cost. No specific scheme's figures are verified in this run.

## Action checklist

- **Plan:** use only the Direct Plan (TER 0.84% vs 1.79% [C1961][C1962]).
- **Existing holders:** keep holdings and SIPs running. Selling after the recent -4.89% fall [C2008] would lock in the loss. Check the exit load [C1963] and your tax position (UNVERIFIED [C1967]) before any switch.
- **New money:** prefer a low-cost midcap index fund [C1965] or a peer with a stronger 5-year record [C2090][C2036][C2043]. Confirm the peer's TER and riskometer from its own AMC first.
- **If you still choose this fund:** invest through a SIP or spread a lump sum over several months. The 10-year worst fall was -29.36% [C1986].
- **Review:** every six months, using the AMC's monthly factsheet. Compare the 3- and 5-year returns with the BSE Midcap 150 TRI [C2015] and with the peers above.
- **What to watch:** the new CIO's first year [C2019], any change of fund manager [C2060], whether mid-cap holdings stay above 65% [C1970][C1976], and the monthly SEBI stress-test disclosure for mid-cap funds.

## Data caveats and sources

- **No primary documents:** no SID, KIM, factsheet or portfolio disclosure is in the document store. The AMC's factsheet PDFs could not be read. All AMC figures come from the AMC's live scheme page, cited by URL.
- **Figures left out as unverified or disputed:**
  - the fund's own Sharpe and Sortino ratios;
  - 10-year volatility and rolling returns;
  - category rank, quartile and medians;
  - trailing benchmark returns and the fund-vs-benchmark gaps;
  - the index-fund vs active-fund comparison since launch;
  - HDFC's volatility and drawdown, and Motilal's drawdown;
  - the manager's other schemes;
  - the reported press shock to a single holding;
  - the CEO's term.
- **Tools unavailable in this revision:** AMFI NAV re-queries and claim saving were not permitted, so none of these could be re-checked. The two TER gaps are fincalc outputs cited to their verified inputs.
- **Marked UNVERIFIED:** peer risk figures, peer TERs, tax rates, holdings count and industry flows.
- **Sources:**
  - AMFI NAV History report, https://portal.amfiindia.com/DownloadNAVHistoryReport_Po.aspx, for NAVs, returns and risk [C1952][C1986];
  - Axis MF scheme page, https://www.axismf.com/mutual-funds/equity-funds/axis-mid-cap-fund/mc-dg/direct, for TER, AUM, portfolio and managers [C1961][C1968][C2060];
  - SEBI final order page for the front-running case [C2017];
  - Value Research on the CIO change [C2019];
  - Upstox on the exit-load addendum [C2072].
- All accessed on 2026-09-29 (IST) [C1952].

*Personal research, not SEBI-registered advice. Past returns do not guarantee future returns.*
